name: Dong-Geun Kim
bio: I am a Ph.D. candidate in the Interaction Lab at POSTECH. My research is on vibrotactile perception and tactile communication: how well people can identify and localize vibration patterns on the forearm, and how those patterns can be used to carry information. Right now I am building a tactile Korean system for people with visual or hearing impairments. I have also worked on mid-air ultrasonic haptics and on matching sounds to touch.

research.name: Tactile communication
research.description: Delivering text and other information through vibration patterns on the forearm, so it can be read by touch.

research.name: Vibrotactile perception
research.description: Measuring how the number, placement, and timing of tactors change what people can identify and where they feel it.

research.name: Mid-air haptics
research.description: Making weak ultrasonic mid-air stimuli feel stronger and easier to recognize by adding vibration at the wrist.

education.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH)
education.degree: Integrated M.S./Ph.D. in IT Convergence Engineering

education.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST)

experience.description: Developed high-frequency ultrasound transducers for tactile applications.

projects.name: Tactile Korean System for the Visually and Hearing Impaired (PM)
projects.description: Developing a way to deliver Korean text through a wearable vibrotactile array, for people with visual or hearing impairments.

projects.name: Mid-air Haptic Rendering for Digital Twin (PM)
projects.description: Real-time mid-air haptic rendering for digital twins. Studied how wrist vibration raises the perceived intensity of weak ultrasonic stimuli and improves pattern recognition.

projects.name: Investigating the Luxuriousness of Haptic Warning
projects.description: User studies on steering-wheel vibration warnings and what makes them feel luxurious.

projects.name: Performance Metric for User Experience
projects.description: Metrics for user experience in digital environments, including sound-to-touch matching for short sounds.

projects.name: Multimodal Haptic Tool for AR Sports
projects.description: MMGrip, a handheld device that combines vibration, impact, and shear to render contact realistically.
